structured.answer: Open an account at פסגות and buy the fund "אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)". The page says I'd have about 86,045 ₪ after 10 years. That's with the page's own numbers, 10,000 ₪ now and 500 a month at 7%, which I didn't change.

stuck.why: They were already set to 10,000 and 500, not my 30,000. I left them alone, so the 86,045 isn't really my number.
It says '−1,030 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם'. For a second I read the minus as losing money, not as 'less than your choice'.
'18 ₪ יותר' for the account and '1,390 ₪ פחות' for the fund. I couldn't tell whether more or less was the good one here.
Every fund has a minus percent, like −0.04% or −0.37%. That looks like losing money, even though the top one is the 'choice'.

findings.what: Every fund shows a minus percent (−0.04%, −0.54%). It reads like the funds lose money. Nothing next to the number says what it means.
The comparison numbers come with a minus (−1,030 ₪, −1,733 ₪) right where a loss would go. It's scary until you work out it means 'less than the top one'.
findings.where: Screen 2 second card, fund list left column

findings.what: The calculator starts at 10,000 + 500, so the big result isn't my money. The first big number (70,000) sticks in my head anyway.
Every bank row repeats the same grey 'לא בחישוב' box with a long list of who gets other prices. I have to read past it each time to get to the number.
The fee colours are explained once in a legend. After that I have to keep going back to match the bar colours in each row.
findings.where: Screen 3 legend vs bars in screens 4–6

findings.what: '18 ₪ יותר' and '1,390 ₪ פחות' sit next to each other. It's not clear which one is good for me.
Every fund card repeats the same tags (קרן סל, מחזיקה את המניות). They're cut off at the left edge, so I can't read them fully.
